summary.text:
A quarterly monitoring paper that carries the borrowing table, the maturity structure, the counterparty list, the full investments schedule and the prudential indicators — and stops there. There is no CFR, no other long-term liabilities, no internal borrowing figure, no MRP policy, no financing-cost ratio, no premium/discount narrative. The balance-sheet identity cannot be closed from this paper alone; that would need the annual outturn or the TMSS, neither of which we currently hold for Bolton.

What the paper does show ties cleanly. External borrowing is £158.000m — £118.000m PWLB and £40.000m market loans, all fixed rate, no short-term debt. The maturity profile puts the whole £158m at 25 years and above: £20m in 25-30 years, £118m in 30-35 years and £20m at 50 years and above. That £118m 30-35 year bucket is our two PWLB loans exactly — £100m at 2.55% to 2 November 2057 and £18m at 2.64% to 8 November 2058 — matching to the pound. Weighted rate 2.56% by our arithmetic; the paper doesn't print a rate.

The other side is the more distinctive thing. Appendix 3 shows £134.850m of investments, of which £120.000m is out on 15 short-term loans to 14 different councils at rates from 4.20% to 4.85% — weighted average 4.48% by our arithmetic. Weighted average life is 9.35 weeks. On the whole PWLB book, that is roughly 192 basis points of positive carry from cheap long money into the LA-to-LA market. Bolton is visibly one of the larger cash lenders on that market in our library, sitting on the other side from several councils whose papers we already hold (Liverpool, Manchester, Cornwall and others among the counterparties).

No email addresses are published in the paper — Report of and Reporting Officer are both Graeme Wilson, Borough Treasurer (S151); Contact Officer is Lisa Melia, Career Grade Principal Accountant - Corporate. Any send is address-blocked until we find one.

officer.body:
Hi Graeme,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the Q4 report that went to the Executive Cabinet Member - Deputy Leader on 8 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

A cross-check first, and yours ties two ways. Your §2.2.1 PWLB row of £118,000,000 is our file for Bolton exactly: two MATURITY loans, £100m at 2.55% out to 2 November 2057 and £18m at 2.64% out to 8 November 2058. The two together also equal your §2.7.3 30-35 year maturity bucket at £118,000,000 to the pound, so the two tables agree independently. We don't hold your £40m of market loans, so the £20m in your 25-30 year bucket and the £20m in the 50+ bucket sit outside our view — no comment we can add there.

The reason we wrote is the shape of what you have. Your PWLB is at a weighted 2.56% by our arithmetic and locked well past most people's careers — the earliest maturity is 2057, and it is 100% fixed. Of the PWLB books we have priced this summer, that is one of the cheapest long-dated positions in our library. New PWLB at those maturities today on the DMO's certainty curve, notice 314/26, is around 6.4% (25-year at 6.46%, 50-year at 6.27%, and your book sits between them). So the rates you locked are running roughly 380 basis points below where the equivalent new borrowing would price today.

The other side is the more distinctive part. Appendix 3 shows £120m of cash out on 15 short-term loans to 14 different councils at rates from 4.20% to 4.85%, weighted average 4.48% by our arithmetic (you don't print an average). Weighted average life 9.35 weeks. So on the whole PWLB book you are running roughly 192 basis points of positive carry from cheap long money into the inter-authority market. Of the councils we read, most report the reverse — short PWLB against longer LA money — and only a handful of substantial cash lenders like yours appear consistently on the other side.

That inter-authority market is one we watch closely; the sector-wide monthly breakdown of every PWLB draw, and the daily rate paths, sit at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity, and it is where you can see thin months coming — when the wholesale side goes thin, LA-to-LA rates move most.

On pricing: your two PWLB loans on the DMO's premature repayment curve today sit around £52m below par, because rates at those maturities have moved a long way since. Standard caveats and we mean them — we don't sell treasury products, we model no MRP or accounting treatment, and only the DMO can quote. Yours is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

On training, three fit Bolton. Intra-LA borrowing & lending markets is directly on point given the £120m book. PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator for the pricing on your two long loans. And Liquidity & cashflow forecasting for a treasury book whose weighted average life is measured in weeks. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
